facts.fact: The electoral roll for the 19 July 2026 presidential election was compiled automatically from civil registry (DGRN) data under the EU-funded PRESE, and the provisional roll holds 146,510 voters, per the CEN president.
The provisional roll is open for public consultation from 1 to 8 August 2026 at district, regional and diaspora electoral commissions and online on the CEN website, per the CEN president.
The roll for the 19 July 2026 presidential election was compiled automatically from data of the civil registry directorate (DGRN) for the first time.

A platform for automatic and permanent voter registration is being developed under the EU-funded PReSE with the Universidade de Aveiro, and the electoral database is being consolidated, per the project coordinator.

facts.fact: A campaign is under way to consolidate the electoral registration database using interoperability with the civil registry databases, says the PReSE coordinator.

facts.fact: The EU-funded PReSE, implemented through Camoes I.P., aims to set up an automatic and permanent electoral registration system, with an interoperability platform between the civil registry database (SIGA and Bilhete de Identidade) and the electoral roll database being developed by the University of Aveiro.

The National Data Protection Agency will supervise personal data during the connection between the civil registry and notary databases and the CEN database for the automatic electoral registration for the 2026 elections, per its president.

The new electoral registration law, in force after publication on 26 March 2026, enters citizens in the electoral database ex officio at 18 on the basis of DGRN civil identification data shared with the CEN, per the PReSE.

note: Says the ID card will become the base document for automatic voter registration, but states no register under way, in service, open to check or linked yet.

facts.fact: Camoes reports that an automatic voter registration platform, under development by the Universidade de Aveiro, was presented at a public session on 4 September 2025.
The DGRN director says the automatic voter-registration platform, built under the EU-funded PReSE, is 98% ready and due to be tested in January 2026, pending legal review before the 2026 elections.
The Portuguese cooperation note says the platform interoperates the civil register database (SIGA and Bilhete de Identidade) with the electoral register database so voters are enrolled automatically.
PReSE, EU-financed and implemented by Camoes, is developing through the Universidade de Aveiro an automatic and permanent electoral registration system, with staff trained to maintain it.

facts.fact: The National Electoral Commission (CEN) says 142,298 voters are enrolled for the 19 July 2026 presidential election, on a roll compiled automatically for the first time.
The CEN says the roll was compiled automatically from the Direcção dos Registos Civis database, though many people were left out.

The PReSE project says the automatic electoral registration platform built by the University of Aveiro is operational and already used to draw up the provisional 2026 electoral rolls in Sao Tome and Principe.

The PReSE project says the platform makes civil registry data and the electoral registration database interoperable, updating voters automatically, with the DGRN removing duplicate records and deceased citizens from the electoral database.
